article_ref: SI 2009/890, regs. 9, 26 (portable, via scheme) and regs. 42-45 (industrial/automotive, direct)
title: United Kingdom: battery producer registration
summary: A producer placing batteries on the UK market, including batteries inside products, must register as a battery producer. A tonnage threshold determines whether registration is direct or through a scheme. Flagged in v1; the full module is v2.

sources.title: The Waste Batteries and Accumulators Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/890)
sources.note: Fetched the statute directly. The 1-tonne threshold is confirmed, but only for PORTABLE batteries: reg. 2 defines a 'small producer' as one placing 1 tonne or less of portable batteries on the market per year; reg. 9 requires non-small portable-battery producers to join a compliance scheme, and reg. 26 covers registration of scheme members and small producers via that scheme. Industrial and automotive batteries are a SEPARATE, thresholdless track: reg. 42 requires direct registration with the Secretary of State for any producer placing industrial/automotive batteries on the market, 'with effect from 16th October 2009', regardless of tonnage. This row's applies_when (product.has_battery, no battery-type distinction) does not separate the two tracks -- not a correctness bug (both tracks require *some* form of registration, so the row is not wrong to say registration applies), but the specific registration route and threshold shown to a customer should differ by battery type; not modelled this pass. DATE FIX: effective_from was 2010-01-01; the general commencement of these Regulations is 5 May 2009 (reg. 1(2)), and the specific registration duties (regs. 26, 42) took effect on 15/16 October 2009 -- a full quarter earlier than drafted. Corrected to 2009-10-15.
